picks.what: View of the town (“Sabaxar”), engraving in Nicolaes Witsen’s Noord en Oost Tartarye
picks.why: earliest view of the town: wooden walls and churches above the Volga; caption line trimmed

picks.who: Ivan Bugreev, after drawings by Alexei Svechin and Mikhail Makhaev
picks.why: general view across the river, churches and bell towers along the skyline

picks.what: View of the old town and its churches, photograph
picks.why: exactly dated photo; the old town’s cathedral and bell towers recognizable; mount trimmed

gaps: P0–P1: nothing; P5: only 1960 snapshots of a sign-lined road, a river station with a couple and a rotunda; P6: existing view kept (#17 is a modern-district view, not better)
notes: #2: Commons gives only ‘17th century’; the description dates Witsen’s book to 1692 (its plates may have appeared only in the 1705 second edition). #1 (‘1733’) is the same composition as #5 in a poorer, uncertainly dated copy, so skipped. #10 (color painting from across the Volga, credited to Fyodor Vasilyev, 1870s) is a weaker P4 alternative: only 800 px and the town is small and distant.
